text:
Grace Kim: Want to settle the open design question for selector v2: do we go fully table-driven (registry keyed by model_family x seq_bucket x gpu_sku) or do we keep heuristic layering (if/else rules + a couple override knobs)?

Grace Kim: Context: v1 is mostly heuristics and it’s getting brittle as we add families + new SKUs. Table gives determinism + easier benchmarking, but I’m worried about table maintenance / missing coverage.

Noah Patel: +1 table-driven. Every time we “just add one more heuristic” we’re encoding a benchmark result in code and hiding the assumptions.

Noah Patel: The failure mode of heuristics is also worse: it looks like it’s “working” until a new GPU/model combo hits a path we never exercised.

Hiro Tanaka: Table-driven sounds nice, but we’re not going to have complete data for every combo. With heuristics we at least have a sensible default based on capabilities (SM, shared mem, etc).

Yuki Sato: I think it’s not either/or. Table-driven for the top N families we care about, plus a *small* heuristic fallback when there’s no entry.

Yuki Sato: But the fallback has to be explicit + safe. Not “random best guess.”

Sofia Ivanova: from scheduling side: we can provide better signals (prefill vs decode regime, effective ctx bucket). That makes table entries more stable. Heuristics today are mixing scheduling context assumptions implicitly.

Grace Kim: If we do hybrid, how do we prevent the fallback heuristics from becoming the de facto path (and hiding missing table entries)?

Noah Patel: Make missing table coverage noisy.
- Metric: selector_table_miss{model_family, gpu_class, seq_bucket}
- Counter in canary dashboards
- Optional “fail closed” in perf-lab so new families can’t ship without entries

Hiro Tanaka: I’m still nervous about the operational burden. Who updates the table? How do we review it? I don’t want kernel engineers paging because the registry missed some corner.

Omar El-Sayed: table ops is actually *better* if we do it like “kernel registry schema + versioning” and gate changes. With heuristics, any code change = runtime release + risk.

Omar El-Sayed: also remember the incident in Nov where a heuristic change for A10 long-context silently flipped decode kernel for a model family we didn’t benchmark? Took us 2 days to even identify the pivot.

Grace Kim: yeah, that was the “A10 p95 blew up for long prompts but only in mixed batches” thing.

Yuki Sato: ^ that’s exactly the kind of thing a table + telemetry would catch immediately.

Hiro Tanaka: But that incident was also about missing observability, not table vs heuristics.

Noah Patel: It was both. The heuristics were doing “if gpu_has_x then prefer kernel K3” and it applied to more shapes than intended.

Noah Patel: With a table you encode the intent: “Mistral-family + decode + long + A10 => K2” and nothing else.

Lena Fischer: +1 on explicit. Also re: seq buckets: if we’re going to wire buckets from scheduler, we should treat bucket boundaries as API. Heuristic code tends to sneak in different boundaries.

Grace Kim: ok. Let me ask a sharper question: if we pick table-driven, do we still allow heuristic tie-breakers *within* a cell? e.g. based on exact head_dim or GQA flag.

Yuki Sato: that should be part of the model_family taxonomy / flags, not a hidden tie-breaker. Otherwise the table stops being a table.

Noah Patel: agree. Define model_family as (arch + key flags). Keep it coarse, but not so coarse that half the family behaves differently.

Hiro Tanaka: Practical issue: we don’t always have model metadata cleanly. Some customers bring weird configs.

Noah Patel: then the table key should include “unknown/partial metadata” as a first-class family => safe set.

Noah Patel: Also: ADR exists for this. Can we align on it? I don’t want us relitigating every week.

Grace Kim: link?

Noah Patel: ADR-0147 draft: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ARCH/ADR-0147+Kernel+selector+v2+table-driven+registry

Grace Kim: reading now.

Thomas Baird: jumping in from metrics/cardinality angle: if we keep heuristics in code, we tend to log high-cardinality “reason” strings.

Thomas Baird: Table-driven enables controlled labels: selector_version, registry_version, kernel_id, gpu_class, seq_bucket, model_family (bucketed). Please don’t add per-branch “why” labels.

Grace Kim: good call.

Connor O'Brien: release POV: table-driven registry w/ versioning is easier to roll back quickly.

Connor O'Brien: If a registry version is bad, we can flip back without reverting runtime binaries (depending on how we ship it). If it’s in code, rollback = redeploy runtime.

Hiro Tanaka: Are we shipping the registry as config or compiled in?

Noah Patel: Proposed: registry is a versioned artifact shipped with runtime (for now) + optional remote override for emergency (but locked down).

Yuki Sato: + emergency override path needs guardrails. Otherwise people will “just override” and we’ll never fix root causes.

Omar El-Sayed: For v2, at minimum we need precedence order:
1) emergency kill switch (force v1)
2) per-model-family override (force kernel X)
3) registry lookup
4) safe fallback (minimal kernel set)

Grace Kim: + deterministic tie-breaker: if multiple entries match (e.g. gpu_sku normalized -> gpu_class), pick most specific.

Sofia Ivanova: also need to keep scheduler integration minimal. I can expose seq_bucket + phase (prefill/decode) without big changes, but I can’t support “exact prompt length” plumbing everywhere.

Grace Kim: that’s fine. Table keys will be coarse buckets.

Hiro Tanaka: still feels like a lot of ceremony vs adding 2-3 heuristics and calling it done.

Noah Patel: we’ve tried that. v1 *is* 2-3 heuristics… repeated ~20 times.

Noah Patel: And we have a pattern of regressions when we add a new family:
- unknown model metadata path triggers default kernel
- default kernel is tuned for Llama-ish shapes
- on a new arch it either regresses or (worse) hits correctness edge case

Grace Kim: + we literally had the NaN scare last quarter with the fused attention kernel under a weird head_dim.

Hiro Tanaka: yep.

Mateo Alvarez: catching up. Strong preference: table-driven + explicit fallback. We need predictability across GPU transitions and this is exactly the kind of “inference serving maturity” work we need.

Mateo Alvarez: Also: if we keep heuristics, we’re making it harder for SRE to set guardrails. Table + telemetry gives clear blast radius.

Grace Kim: ok. seems like direction is table-driven registry w/ heuristic fallback as safe set only (not performance-optimized), plus metrics on table misses.

Yuki Sato: +1. Can we also make sure the fallback is *conservative* (known-correct kernels) and doesn’t try to be “fast.”

Omar El-Sayed: We can codify that as “safe kernel set” and require conformance tests for anything outside safe set.

Thomas Baird: pls include a hard rule: no logging the full gpu_sku string; normalize to gpu_class (L4/A10/A100/H100) or we’ll explode cardinality.

Grace Kim: ack. We’ll normalize via Yuki’s SKU mapping.

Grace Kim: Action item: I’ll update the design doc section and cite ADR-0147. Hiro, can you review that we’re not painting kernel team into a maintenance corner?

Hiro Tanaka: yes. If we document ownership + update process (who approves registry changes, perf evidence required), I’m ok.

Connor O'Brien: and we should explicitly mention “registry change requires benchmark-lab evidence + perf-canary thresholds” in the ADR / design.

Grace Kim: noted.

Grace Kim: dropping a strawman registry snippet here (names TBD):
```yaml
registry_version: 3
entries:
  - model_family: llama_gqa
    phase: prefill
    seq_bucket: s0_0_512
    gpu_class: a100
    kernel_id: attn_prefill_k7
  - model_family: llama_gqa
    phase: decode
    seq_bucket: s3_4096_8192
    gpu_class: a10
    kernel_id: attn_decode_k2
fallback:
  kernel_set: safe
```

Yuki Sato: looks right. gpu_class should come from normalized map (incl MIG reporting as base SKU class).

Sofia Ivanova: seq_bucket naming: please keep it stable + aligned w scheduler buckets. I don’t want runtime defining its own buckets.

Grace Kim: yep. We’ll source buckets from scheduler constants.

Mateo Alvarez: thanks all. Let’s move forward w table-driven. If we hit a wall on coverage, we can revisit, but the default should be explicit + data-driven.

Grace Kim: :thumbsup: will update design + ping when ready.

(Grace Kim added :thumbsup: to Mateo Alvarez’s message)

(Connor O'Brien added :white_check_mark: to Grace Kim’s message)

Thomas Baird: one more thing: please add metric for registry_version and selector_version so we can break down latency by decision engine.

Grace Kim: will do.
